newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: INTERVIEW - TVI expects profit by 1998.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - TVI expects profit by 1998.

text.p: Private Portuguese television station TVI-Televisao Independente should begin to turn a profit in 1998 after reaching operational break-even next year, TVI president Carlos Monjardino said.
"If interest rates come down a bit more and inflation stays between 2.5 and 3.0 percent, we can expect TVI to make a profit in 1998," Monjardino told Reuters in an interview.
"But we still have cost-cutting to do," he added.
In 1995 the station, which began operating in 1993 and has never made a profit, posted a loss of 4.85 billion escudos ($31.4 million).
"1997 is the year in which we want to put our house in order once and for all," he said, adding that he expected TVI to break even on the operational side next year.

According to a source close to the company, TVI made an operating profit before tax of 770 million escudos in the first half of 1996, up more than 700 percent from the same period last year. The source said operating costs had fallen by one billion escudos, or 26 percent, in the first half.
Monjardino said TVI was still looking for a strategic partner to take a stake of up to 25 percent by March next year.

"I'd like a strategic partner that would take up to 25 percent and would carry some weight as far as programming is concerned, as well as having a say in the running of the company as a whole," he said.
He said TVI had been in contact with SBS-Scandinavian Broadcasting System SA, Dutch-South African pay television group Nethold and a third potential partner within the European Union.
SBS president Howard Knight said recently that TVI was viable but had lost its way and "needed a captain."
"I do not accept that TVI has lost its bearings as some people have said," Monjardino said.
In July TVI's AGM approved a capital reduction to 9.76 billion escudos from 17.75 billion followed by an increase of 8.2 billion escudos through the creation of 8.2 million new shares.
As a result TVI's shares have been suspended from the Lisbon bourse since July 19.
The capital reduction has already taken place but U.K. funds Morgan Grenfell, Mercury and Fidelity, which jointly hold 35 percent of TVI but were not able to vote, have blocked the capital increase.

"For those interested in buying TVI the (capital increase) obviously makes no sense," Monjardino said. "But I think it's the best way to resolve TVI's problems. I can't propose a big capital reduction just to please a new shareholder," he added.
He said SBS had proposed a capital reduction of between 3.0 and 3.5 billion escudos.

"The U.K. funds have proposed that the directors of TVI, the Portuguese shareholders and the potential strategic partner (SBS) or another submit another proposal to an extraordinary general assembly to get us out of this impasse."
Monjardino said the station's new autumn/winter programming, which cost around 3.0 billion escudos, would allow it to gain 20 percent audience share next year, up from around 15 percent at present.
"Our aim is to provide high quality popular television and to have audience share of between 20 and 25 percent," he said.
